characters.name: Orange
characters.description: Absurd Phobia: He seems to have a huge fear... of dancing hippos. The Ace: Weirdly enough, he is very skilled at doing weird actions. He can also show natural skills when needed, particularly in setting up pranks. Achilles' Heel:Dancing hipposare the one thing that can keep him at bay. And according to the opening ofAsk Orange #82, being forced to not make fun of someone (which is his entire characterization) causes him to literally explode. Adaptational Nice Guy: InHigh Fructose Adventures, while he still makes jokes and can be his usual obnoxious self, he's a lot nicer than he ever was in the web series, willingly helping people with their problems rather than just mostly sitting by and driving them insane. He has even saved the world on occasion. Ambiguously Bi: Despite clearly having a crush on Passion Fruit, Orange has attempted to kiss Pear at least twice, while one episode of Ask Orange has a skit where he and Pear have a baby.

characters.name: Pear
characters.description: Achievements in Ignorance: By refusing to hand over the whistling pinwheel, he ended up buying enough time for the real Future Orange to arrive and kill the Evil Space Warlord. Ascended Extra: Started off as little more than a gag character until he started to make more appearances throughout 2010, all but cementing himself as the deuteragonist by the end of that year. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Pear can barely tolerate Orange and his antics, but deep down, he cares for him and would be devastated if somethingreallybad were to happen to him.In "Jar Jar Stinks", he outright admits that he misses the energy the real one brought to the kitchen and would rather put up with his Orange than the latter's demonic, evil analog counterpart, and sets about to rescue him. Berserk Button:Orange going off-topic on theHOW2episodes annoys him very much. TNT is also a pretty big one for him.Thanks toFlanderization,the very presence of Orange himselfseems to be becoming this in recent years. Orange going off-topic on theHOW2episodes annoys him very much. TNT is also a pretty big one for him.

characters.name: Little Apple
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Originally a gag character, who wasn’t even the focus of his debut episode, he positioned himself as one of the core cast members around his very next appearance in "Wazzup 3: Bonsai Tree". Berserk Button:Early in the series' run, calling him "Midget Apple" will cause him to angrily respond with "It's Little Apple!". As the series progressed though, that button eventually disappeared and his new button became just making fun of his size in general.He also doesn't like jokes being made towards his blatant illiteracy. Early in the series' run, calling him "Midget Apple" will cause him to angrily respond with "It's Little Apple!". As the series progressed though, that button eventually disappeared and his new button became just making fun of his size in general. He also doesn't like jokes being made towards his blatant illiteracy. Catchphrase:The usual one:Character X:[insert sentence that has "Midget Apple" in it here]Midget Apple:Hey! It's Little Apple!(or a variation of that)A less frequently used one is "neato burrito" (his favorite phrase of all time) which originated on hisFacebookandTwitterpages.

characters.name: Marshmallow
characters.description: Alien Among Us: TheHigh Fructose Adventuresepisode "Marshmalia" reveals that they're from the planet Marshmalia. All-Loving Hero: They get along witheveryone, even theirevil teddy bearinOrange Nya-Nya Style. Ambiguous Gender: For a good 12 years this was their primaryRunning Gag, until"PRIDE"finally answered the question: they arenon-binary. Ascended Extra: They started off as Jigsaw's victim-turned-tormentor alongside Orange in the second "Jigsaw" episode, but "Wishful Thinking" onwards elevated them to one of the core five characters. Badass Adorable: They are a small, kind marshmallow who is cheerful all the time, and yet they managed to survive many life-threatening situations as well as being capable of roughing up any unfortunate food that makes them pissed.

characters.name: Passion Fruit
characters.description: Action Girl:Annoying Orange vs Angry Birds: PASSION FRUITreveals her to be a black belt. Character Blog: She's onFacebook,Twitter, and theofficial blog. Closer to Earth: DuringThe Exploding Orange, while Orangehas the hiccups:Passion Fruit:Look, everybody. The important thing right now is to just remain calm.(Orange hiccups)(Everyone freaks out)Passion Fruit:No, no, NO! Everybody just shut up! Damsel in Distress:Analog Orange turns her into an Orcux and holds her captive in the final episode of his epnymous saga to force the real Orange into aSadistic Choice. Fortunately, he, Pear, and Grapefruit find a loophole. Inconsistent Spelling: Her name is occasionally listed as one word ("Passionfruit").

characters.name: Grapefruit
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: Grapefruit prides himself as a ladies' man, but his attempts to impress them frequently fall flat and end up making him a bigger fool out of himself. Passionnotehis initial target of affectionand Sisnotehis latest target of affectionhave both lampshaded this many times:Passion:(duringa "The Juice" episode in Christmasafter Grapefruit tries hitting on her)On behalf of ladies everywhere... eh,no. Adaptational Villainy: InHigh Fructose Adventures, he takes on an active role as the antagonist in a couple of episodes, most notably in "Fruit-Vengers", where he is shown brutally murdering vegetables with his telekinetic powers. Ascended Extra: He was originally a one-shot antagonist who got knifed after his debut, but after he was revived in "Frankenfruit", and givenA Day in the Limelightin "Best Fiends Forever", he became one of the five core main characters with his own spotlight episodes. Back from the Dead: InFrankenfruit, despite appearing alive in the earlier episodesLiam the Leprechaun - Liam Vs. Grapefruit! (Characters From the Annoying Orange!)andLiam the Leprechaun - Lousy Limericks. Bad Liar: Mostly on hisFacebookandTwitterpages, but occasionally in the series as well.

characters.name: Grandpa Lemon
characters.description: Back from the Dead: InFrankenfruit. Character Blog: He's onFacebookandTwitter. Cool Old Guy: He rides motorcycles and even does motorcycle jumps. Gasshole: Grandpa Lemon is known for how flatulent he is. Posthumous Character: InOrange Potter and the Deathly Apple, as Grandpa Lemondore, he only appears in aDead Person Conversationwith Orange Potter.

characters.name: Orange's Sister (Sis)
characters.description: Distaff Counterpart: Orange, but a girl. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Despite being just as annoying as her brother, she's much nicer than him by comparison.

characters.name: Squash
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Like some of the other recurring characters, he was initially a one-off joke before becoming a prominent character, unlike the other cases of this in the series, he is mostly used as a gag character that shows up to kill another character via squashing them, much to his dismay. Catchphrase: "Ewww gross!" Character Blog: He's onFacebookandTwitter. The Eeyore: You can tell how sad he is when he squashes things. Expy: Of the Squash fromPlants vs. Zombies. His "Fruits vs Zombies" video even has him substituting forPvZ's Squash.

characters.name: Apple
characters.description: Ambiguous Situation: It's unclear if this character is the same Apple from the first episode or if he's the Apple from Kitchen Carnage. Ascended Extra: He was initially just a character who debuted in the very first episode, however, he became a frequently recurring character to the point he is arguably becoming a part of the main cast. Butt-Monkey: Compared to other characters, who at least survive some of their reappearances, this guy barely comes out alive in most of the episodes that focus on him. Canon Foreigner: Unless it's the same apple from the original Annoying Orange short, that is. They Killed Kenny Again: He dies a lot of times, yet whenever he appears once more, he doesn't seem to be scathed in the slightest.

characters.name: Nude Dude
characters.description: An apple who had its skin peeled off and happily walks around the kitchen without it. Birds of a Feather: He gets along swimmingly with Orange and loves to be as annoying as him. Naked People Are Funny: His whole ordeal is that he is naked. They Killed Kenny Again: In a fair amount of his appearances, Nude Dude gets killed in some way at the end. In his first appearance, he is cut up by knife. In his second, he is eaten by a werewolf. In his third, and apple bobber bites him.

characters.name: Lou the Tick
characters.description: A conspiracy theorist tick who resides in a tinfoil tent. Cloudcuckoolander: He is highly erratic and makes strange assumptions about what is affecting the current situation. Conspiracy Theorist: He has a ton of outrageous conspiracies relating to the current situation.Sometimes he turns out to be right. A Day in the Limelight: He got to host a Top 5 list for Shocktober 2017. Insane Troll Logic: Most of his conspiracies rely on this. For instance, he believes thatSteven Spielbergdeceived the general public into believing dinosaurs exist based on the huge box office success ofJurassic Park (1993).

characters.name: Corey
characters.description: Little Apple's thrill-seeking half-brother. Berserk Button: Don't call him "yellow". That man is willing to take another knife if it means avoiding ridicule. Beyond the Impossible: Getting cut in half means imminent death for any fruit. Cory managedto survive this at the cost of half of his brain. Blessed with Suck: The good thing about getting cut in half is that you lose half of your brain, getting rid of some attributes you probably dislike. The bad thing?You're still losing half of your brain, so while Corey lost the half that controlled his fear, he also lost some more useful attributes, like the part that allows him to breathe and the part that allowed him to do basic math. Fearless Fool: Lost the part of his brain that controls fear.

characters.name: Knife
characters.description: Affably Evil:While calling "evil" is a bit stretch since he's not even evil at all, he's the most famous weapon in this franchise that killed a lot of fruits, but in "No More Mr. Knife Guy", it's revealed that he's actuallyaffable and friendlyand hates cutting things in half. Animate Inanimate Object: The vast majority of the time, he's faceless, being used asHe Who Must Not Be Seen's tool to cut up food. "No More Mr. Knife Guy" marks his first role as a character rather than an object. Big Bad: While the series isn't heavy on continuity (aside from the GG arc and the Analog Orange arc), Knife is the closest thing to a major antagonist throughout the episodes and is responsible for most of the character deaths. Character Blog: He's onFacebookandTwitter. My God, What Have I Done?: He heavily dislikes it when he cuts things and asks: "I did it again, didn't I?" in a remorseful tone.

characters.name: Analog Orange
characters.description: Arc Villain: Of the Analog Orange Saga. Asshole Victim:This orange is so vile and murderous that you don't need to feel bad for him when he got killed via Supernova Explosion. Capture and Replicate:He pulled this off on the original Orange, trapping him in a jar in the VHS Dimension while Analog takes his place in order to kill more fruits while posing as him. Card-Carrying Villain: In his final appearance (Orcrux #4: THE FINAL BATTLE), he admits that he's super evil, loves being evil, and is never going to stop being evil. Defeat Equals Explosion: Exaggerated.After getting annoyed to death, he doesn't just explode, rather, in Orange's words, he outrightsupernova'd.

characters.name: Liam the Leprechaun
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: Is humiliated and/or killed in almost every single one of his appearances. Catchphrase:"Aw crap!". InThe Leprechaun Trap, he changes it to "Awtrap!" at Orange's suggestion to be more in line with the titular trap.He also tends to say "You got it!" just before granting wishes. "Aw crap!". InThe Leprechaun Trap, he changes it to "Awtrap!" at Orange's suggestion to be more in line with the titular trap. He also tends to say "You got it!" just before granting wishes. Character Blog: He's onFacebookandTwitter.

characters.name: Clover
characters.description: Gasshole: Can be this at times, but he does it on purpose. Non-Standard Character Design: He's "played" by a cartoon clover leaf rather than a real one.

characters.name: Mustachios
characters.description: Accidental Misnaming: The ones inMystery of the Mustachios. Character Blog: They're onFacebookandTwitter. Paper-Thin Disguise: InMystery of the Mustachios, Orange and Pear immediately recognize them as Pistachios, but the Pistachio-eating human apparently was fooled. Product Placement: The ones inMystery of the Mustachiosare specifically Wonderful Pistachios, and their bag appears prominently at the beginning of the episode.

characters.name: ZOOM Energy Drink
characters.description: Character Blog: He's onFacebookandTwitter. Eyeless Face: His face lacks eyes. Klatchian Coffee: One sip of Zoom juice can load anyone with a lot of energy. Alot. Orange spent 10 hours talking and making noises in high speed after Zoom accidentally spilled all of his contents into his mouth in his debut episode. The can himself admits that his drink can cause extreme behavior in children. Large Ham: Having a lot of energy, Zoom is one the hammiest characters in the show, and he always speaks in a loud, enthusiastic voice.Zoom:THIS IS EXTREEEEEEEEEEMEEEEEEEE!!! Put on a Bus: Disappeared from the series afterBob Jenz's retirement in 2021.

characters.name: Daneboe
characters.description: As Herself: This fictionalized version of Daneboe is played by Daneboe. Who would've guessed? Catchphrase: "Say no to drugs, say yes to jumping!OriginatedinDoodle Jump: Getting high without drugs, theirLet's PlayofDoodle Jump. Cool Shades: InLaser Pointer Hack! Mad Libs Catchphrase: In her catchphrase, she will sometimes replace "jumping" with other things.

characters.name: Voice
characters.description: Breaking the Fourth Wall: Speaks to both the viewer and the characters. Interactive Narrator: Though he's really more of an announcer. No Name Given: In his firstAnnoying Orangeappearance (The Annoying Trailer) he's called "Voice" by Orange, but other than that he hasn't been named.Johnny the announcer fromFruit For Allsounds the same as Voice, and they may be the same character. Johnny the announcer fromFruit For Allsounds the same as Voice, and they may be the same character.

characters.name: Nerville
characters.description: Character Blog: He's onTwitter. Inconsistent Spelling: His name is misspelled as "Nervil" in the closed captions of "Marshmalia" (despite the correct spelling being listed in the opening credits). Speaks Fluent Animal: He can talk to fruit (which is apparently unusual, despite other humans doing so in the web videos).

characters.name: Other Minor Characters
characters.description: Accidental Misnaming: A common reaction to Orange'sNicknamertendencies. The Alcoholic: Nick Nolte from theNBK 24/7series. Always Someone More Annoying: The other orange fromMore Annoying Orange, who is so annoying that he managed to annoy Orange. Ambiguously Gay: Glitter Groin fromWTF is that?!andASK AARON ANYTHING #1. Annoying Laugh: The other orange fromMore Annoying Orangehas a laugh even more annoying than the original Orange's.
